<a data-pjax="true" title="BUG: Do not scale the text leading by the font size (#3987)

The TL operand is a distance in unscaled text space units (PDF 32000-1,
9.3.5) and T* already applies the text matrix to it, so scaling it by the
font size moved the text matrix by TL * font size per line. This showed up
in the text matrix reported to visitor_text: with 14 TL and a 12 pt font,
the lines were 168 units apart instead of 14.

The scaling was added for #2262, where line breaks were missing. The
actual cause there is in crlf_space_check: the vertical delta is computed
from text matrix x CTM, but was compared against a threshold scaled by the
text matrix alone, so any page whose CTM scales the text down lost its line
breaks. Take the scaling factors from the combined matrices instead, which
fixes #2262 without distorting the leading -- and fixes it for text
positioned by Tm or Td as well, which the TL scaling never covered.

Closes #3982.

<a data-pjax="true" title="BUG: Apply character spacing (Tc) per glyph in layout-mode extraction (#3951)

In layout-mode text extraction, TextStateParams.word_tx added the
character-spacing amount Tc exactly once per shown string, regardless of
how many glyphs the string contained. PDF 32000-1 (9.3.2, 9.4.4) defines
Tc as a per-glyph quantity: showing an N-glyph string advances the text
matrix by N * Tc, and a TJ numeric adjustment (which shows no glyph)
contributes no Tc at all.

The once-per-call term left every multi-glyph TJ string element short by
(N - 1) * Tc, shifting everything after it in the array, and added a
spurious +Tc for the empty TextStateParams used to advance a leading TJ
numeric adjustment. Multiply Tc by len(word), consistent with the
per-glyph width loop directly above and the existing per-space-glyph
Tw term; len("") == 0 drops the spurious term for pure adjustments.

Closes #3948." class="Link--secondary" href="/py-pdf/pypdf/commit/11d92f2e34d101b73eccd7350e4eaabc10ecb6d7">BUG: Apply character spacing (Tc) per glyph in layout-mode extraction (</a>

<a data-pjax="true" title="BUG: Do not scale the text leading by the font size (#3987)

The TL operand is a distance in unscaled text space units (PDF 32000-1,
9.3.5) and T* already applies the text matrix to it, so scaling it by the
font size moved the text matrix by TL * font size per line. This showed up
in the text matrix reported to visitor_text: with 14 TL and a 12 pt font,
the lines were 168 units apart instead of 14.

The scaling was added for #2262, where line breaks were missing. The
actual cause there is in crlf_space_check: the vertical delta is computed
from text matrix x CTM, but was compared against a threshold scaled by the
text matrix alone, so any page whose CTM scales the text down lost its line
breaks. Take the scaling factors from the combined matrices instead, which
fixes #2262 without distorting the leading -- and fixes it for text
positioned by Tm or Td as well, which the TL scaling never covered.

Closes #3982.

<a data-pjax="true" title="BUG: Fix TreeObject.insert_child KeyError on fresh children (#3786)

When inserting a child at the first position, the exception handler
unconditionally deletes child_obj["/Next"]. If the child is a fresh
TreeObject without a "/Next" key, this raises KeyError.

Fix: guard the deletion with a check for the key's existence.

Fixes #3727

Regression test: inserting a fresh TreeObject (no /Next key) into
the first position previously raised a KeyError. This test verifies
the fix: the except branch now guards the /Next deletion with an
'exists' check instead of unconditionally deleting.

Signed-off-by: Abdulazez A. <abzaeko@gmail.com>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto">
<h1 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">pypdf</h1>
<a id="user-content-pypdf" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: pypdf" href="#pypdf">
<svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true">
<path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path>

</a>
</div>
<p dir="auto">
pypdf is a free and open-source pure-python PDF library capable of splitting,

<a href="https://pypdf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/user/merging-pdfs.html" rel="nofollow">merging</a>
,

<a href="https://pypdf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/user/cropping-and-transforming.html" rel="nofollow">cropping, and transforming</a>

the pages of PDF files. It can also add
custom data, viewing options, and

<a href="https://pypdf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/user/encryption-decryption.html" rel="nofollow">passwords</a>

to PDF files. pypdf can

<a href="https://pypdf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/user/extract-text.html" rel="nofollow">retrieve text</a>

and

<a href="https://pypdf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/user/metadata.html" rel="nofollow">metadata</a>

from PDFs as well.
</p>
<p dir="auto">
See 
<a href="https://github.com/py-pdf/pdfly">pdfly</a>
 for a CLI application that uses pypdf to interact with PDFs.
</p>

<p dir="auto">
A good bug ticket includes a MCVE - a minimal complete verifiable example.
For pypdf, this means that you must upload a PDF that causes the bug to occur
as well as the code you're executing with all of the output. Use

<code>print(pypdf.__version__)</code>
 to tell us which version you're using.
</p>
